thread:
maria: raising an incident — multiple hosted customers reporting 5xx/504s and very high tail latency for text-generation endpoints. p95 jumped from ~120ms to 3s+ around 13:42 UTC.

maria: symptoms: high request queue depth, continuous-batching backlog, timeouts from gateway. customers seeing canceled requests and 502/504.

devon: seeing the same on the metrics side: `request.queue_depth` spiking to 380/400 on prod-pool-3, `continuous_batcher_pending` rising and not draining.

kevin: any recent deploys or config changes?

maria: no deploys flagged by deploy-bot since 13:00. autoscaler didn't trigger because pool is at fixed capacity for dedicated workloads — but these are hosted requests hitting shared pools.

jordan: logs from the gateway show repeated `upstream read timeout` and `502` from the inference runtime. Snippet: 
```
[13:42:11] gateway: upstream_read_timeout host=pool-3-worker-42 request_id=abc123 queue_depth=378
[13:42:12] runtime: batcher: backlog_size=74 max_batch_wait_ms=50 queue_depth=378
[13:42:12] runtime: error: pipeline timeout, returning 504 request_id=abc123
```

maria: observability-bot pulled correlated metrics: `queue.wait_time_p95` crossed 1.8s, `runtime.batch_latency_p99` spiked to 2.7s.

ben: any tenant-specific spikes? who are the top customers in this window?

maria: top impacted tenants: [acme-corp, pixl-ai, sendfast]. acme shows a sudden traffic spike at 13:40 (concurrent requests ~220).

devon: looks like continuous batching is accumulating requests because workers are busy serving large-context jobs. Large-context requests (>=2048 tokens) are longer, blocking batch formation. backlog grows, queue depth limit hits, gateway begins rejecting with 5xx.

kevin: can we repro locally? steps?

jordan: repro sketch: start 200 concurrent clients hitting 
```
for i in {1..200}; do 
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"model":"redwood-large-quant","input":"<~2k tokens>"}' &
done
```
should see queue_depth climb and occasional 502/504. also reproducible with `wrk` or `hey -n 2000 -c 200`.

maria: mitigation options (short-term):
- temporarily lower `max_batch_wait_ms` from 50 -> 10 on prod-pool-3 so batcher flushes sooner.
- enable tenant-based circuit-breaker for acme-corp to limit concurrency to 20.
- increase worker count for pool-3 by +2 (if capacity available).
- enable fallback routing to `redwood-small-v1` for time-sensitive tenants.

devon: I pushed a canary to reduce `max_batch_wait_ms` to 10 on pool-3-worker-*. observing now.

ops-bot: change accepted: config-update pool-3 max_batch_wait_ms=10 by devon at 13:51 UTC.

maria: also added a temporary per-tenant concurrency cap for acme at 13:52.

jordan: initial effect: queue_depth dropped from 380 -> 120 within two minutes, p95 fell from 3.2s -> 620ms. But batch efficiency decreased slightly (token/sec down ~8%).

kevin: any customer comms? support ticket numbers?

maria: support created escalation tickets: SUP-3489 (acme), SUP-3491 (pixl-ai). I posted a short note to affected customers: "we're seeing transient request queue saturation causing 5xx/timeouts; we're actively applying mitigations and will post follow-up" :thumbsup:.

ben: follow-ups we should do before we close:
- (1) run a root cause analysis: why did the scheduler not preempt large-context jobs?
- (2) consider adding a queue-depth alert threshold at 200 for hosted pools.
- (3) add a tenant spike protection rule to automatically throttle per-tenant concurrency when queue_depth > 150.
- (4) update runbook with explicit steps to reduce `max_batch_wait_ms` and enable fallback routing.

devon: collecting runtime traces and KV cache metrics now. I'll attach traces to the incident ticket.

maria: notes for RCA: continuous batching backlog + large-context hot requests + queue depth limit = gateway timeouts. Contributing factors: no per-tenant throttle for hosted mode, batcher wait tuning optimized for throughput not tail latency.

jordan: post-mitigation plan:
- tune batcher default from 50ms -> 20ms in prod (rollback if token/sec drops too much).
- implement adaptive batch_timeout that lowers wait when queue_depth > X.
- add a prioritized queue for short requests vs long-context requests.

kevin: agree. please create tickets/PRs. assign owners.

maria: creating high-priority tasks now. I'll update incident when RCA draft is ready.

observability-bot: alert cleared for pool-3 queue_depth at 14:05 UTC.

maria: closing the live incident channel for now — we'll keep this open for RCA comments. Thanks team. :heart:
